problems.title: Add Two Numbers
problems.primitivesUsed: DSAExperimentation.DataStructures.SinglyLinkedList.SinglyLinkedListNode<TValue> (same primitive/precedent as MergeTwoSortedListsTests) - single digit-wise carry walk over .Next, dummy-head list building. No new primitive needed since LC2 stores digits least-significant-first, matching the node's natural walk order.
problems.notes: Benchmark compares a BigInteger convert-and-back baseline (O(n^2) due to limb growth on repeated *=10) against the SinglyLinkedListNode digit-wise walk (O(n)); verified via a BenchmarkDotNet dry run showing the gap widen from ~5.8x at Length=200 to ~48x at Length=5000, confirming the real complexity split. All tests pass (7/7 new, 550/551 full suite, 1 pre-existing skip).

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.primitivesUsed: DSAExperimentation.DataStructures.HashMap.HashMap<TKey,TValue> - sliding window tracking each character's last-seen index, jumping the window start past a repeat.
problems.notes: Benchmark compares an O(n^2) brute force (HashSet-per-start-index rescan) against the O(n) HashMap sliding window. Had to fix the initial input generator: a small repeat-heavy alphabet let BruteForce's inner loop break out early (pigeonhole bounds any repeat-free run to the alphabet size), making it look artificially fast; switched to an all-distinct-character string (same 'force the real worst case' convention TwoSumBenchmarks already uses), which exposed the genuine ~24x O(n^2) blowup at Length=5000 in a dry-run smoke test. All tests pass (7/7 new incl. this problem's 4, 550/551 full suite).

problems.title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problems.primitivesUsed: Algorithms.Searching.BinarySearch.LowerBound<Element,TSequence> (generic bisection engine, reused unmodified) composed with a new IRandomAccessSequence<int> witness (PartitionFeasibilitySequence) over the partition index of the smaller array. The witness's Get(i) returns 0 while the partition is feasible and 1 once it isn't - a monotonic 0..0,1..1 sequence, exactly the 'sorted ascending' shape LowerBound already assumes - so LowerBound's existing loop finds the classic O(log(min(m,n))) partition boundary with zero changes to BinarySearch.cs itself. Verified correct against 20,000 randomized cross-checks (vs. concatenate+sort) during development, then removed that scratch fuzz test before finalizing. Benchmark compares this against a MergeAndSort (concatenate + Array.Sort) baseline; dry-run confirmed BinarySearchPartition is both faster and allocation-free at both input sizes.

problems.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.primitivesUsed: Algorithms.StringMatching.Manacher.FindLongestPalindromicSubstring(ReadOnlySpan<char>) - already returns exactly the (Start, Length) bounds this problem asks for; the coverage test is a thin string-slicing wrapper around it, no new algorithmic logic needed. Benchmark compares it against the textbook O(n^2) expand-around-every-center baseline on a small-alphabet (4-letter) random string chosen to make the baseline actually pay its quadratic worst case.
